clue.text: Held during demonstration possibly odd musical instrument

parts.note: kettling is a police tactic of penning protesters in; those held at a demonstration may be kettled
rum is an informal word for strange or odd

explanation.surface: Someone at a protest is detained, perhaps because of some peculiar instrument they were playing.
explanation.walkthrough: Kettling is the British police tactic of corralling demonstrators in a confined area; 'possibly' marks it as one example of being held.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettledrum is a timpani, a large orchestral percussion drum with a bowl-shaped body.

clue.text: Give up keen short-lived interest

definitions.meaning: to ... a habit is to give it up

explanation.surface: Abandoning an enthusiasm that never lasted long.
explanation.definitionFit: Kick means quit (a habit) and also a brief craze or enthusiasm, two separate senses.

clue.text: Unexpected events change courier company

parts.note: to turn is to change, as milk turns
UPS is the parcel delivery firm United Parcel Service

explanation.surface: Surprises follow when a business switches its parcel delivery firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn-up, or turn-up for the books, is a surprising development.

clue.text: German wine, I hear, film club distributed

indicators.note: letters handed out and scattered are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A film society, apparently, is handing out bottles of German wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I hear' looks like a sound-alike signal but is simply part of the letters to be rearranged with FILM CLUB.
explanation.definitionFit: Liebfraumilch is a sweet white Rhine wine, once a popular export from Germany.

clue.text: Scandal in papers upset second princess

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: ID, identity papers
Grace Kelly became Princess Grace of Monaco

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a royal causes a scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Disgrace is shame or a source of public dishonour, much as a scandal is.

clue.text: Two French articles about Charlie, Dad's brother

indicators.note: the articles go around, surrounding the letter for Charlie

parts.note: UN and LE, the French indefinite and definite articles
C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A couple of pieces in a French paper about someone called Charlie, who is a father's sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother of one's father or mother is an uncle.

clue.text: Recalled non-Thatcherite Conservatives in agitated state

indicators.note: called back, so the word runs in the opposite direction

parts.note: Margaret Thatcher called moderate Tories who opposed her policies 'wets'

explanation.surface: Moderate Tories brought back into a party in turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a stew is to be worried and flustered, an idiom for a fretful condition.

clue.text: Afghanistan's rulers seize leader of insurgents, oddly least revolutionary

indicators.note: revolving the whole assembled string turns it back to front

parts.note: to nab is to grab or seize

indicators.note: the leader is the opening letter of the word
taking the odd-numbered letters of the word

explanation.surface: A regime grabs a rebel chief, oddly the least radical of them.
explanation.walkthrough: NAB + I + LAT (odd letters of LEAST) is NABILAT, which 'revolutionary' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taliban is the Islamist movement that has governed Afghanistan since 2021.

clue.text: Deserts wife and son, inspiring various tales

indicators.note: breathing in, so the outer pieces take the rearranged letters inside
in various forms, so the letters come in a different order

explanation.surface: A man abandons his family, making up all sorts of stories as he goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deserts' reads as a verb (abandons) but is the plural noun. 'various' scrambles the tales to ASTEL, which 'inspiring' places inside the wife-and-son frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasteland is barren, uninhabited land, of which a desert is a kind.

clue.text: Told how to make certain characters fancy being fliers

indicators.note: spoken out, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.words: how to make certain characters fancy
parts.note: to curl Us, giving the letter U a decorative flourish

explanation.surface: Instructions for decorative lettering, it seems, to put on a pretty show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curl Us', letters given a flourish, is said like the bird name.
explanation.definitionFit: Curlews are long-billed wading birds, so they are flying creatures.

clue.text: Cloud in Barrow, temperature becoming cold

indicators.note: one letter becomes another, a swap in place

parts.note: a barrow is an ancient burial mound, also called a tumulus
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Weather report: a cloud over the Cumbrian town of Barrow as it turns chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barrow' looks like the town Barrow-in-Furness but is the burial mound.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumulus is the heaped, fluffy white cloud formation seen on fair days.

clue.text: Direct new version of mostly true epic film

parts.note: to motion someone is to direct them with a gesture

indicators.note: a new version reworks the letters into another order
most of the word, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A director makes a fresh adaptation of a largely factual epic film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts TRUE to TRU; 'new version of' rearranges TRU + EPIC as PICTURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Motion picture is a fuller name for a cinema movie.

clue.text: Nat King Cole song, impossible to overlook?

definitions.meaning: the 1951 hit ballad by the American crooner, later a duet with his daughter Natalie
something that cannot be forgotten; overlook in the sense of neglect

explanation.surface: A classic crooner's track that nobody could ignore.
explanation.definitionFit: The song title, and the adjective meaning so memorable it can never slip one's mind.

clue.text: Individualist that's popular in a pub?

definitions.meaning: someone who lives independently of convention
a spirit poured gratis, a free whisky or gin, would go down well at the bar

explanation.surface: A nonconformist character who goes down well at the local.
explanation.definitionFit: A free spirit is an unconventional person; a free spirit is also a complimentary shot of liquor.

clue.text: Investigation concerning main Republican backed by church

indicators.note: followed by, so it sits at the end

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in business letters
the main is the open sea

explanation.surface: An inquiry into an ocean-related matter by a Republican, supported by the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Research is systematic study to find facts, an inquiry.

clue.text: Balkan region rejected Spain's objectionable claims

indicators.note: thrown back, so the run of letters reads in reverse
the phrase holds, or lays claim to, the letters within it

explanation.surface: A Balkan territory dismisses offensive assertions made by Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claims' finds AINSOB inside 'Spain's objectionable', which 'rejected' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosnia is the northern part of Bosnia and Herzegovina, a country in the Balkans.

clue.text: Musical composition from singer, poor kid regularly wearing glasses?

indicators.note: the glasses go on around the other letters, as specs sit on a face

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of spectacles
an informer who sings to the police is a rat

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the phrase

explanation.surface: A bespectacled youngster performs a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: A singer is underworld slang for an informer, here a rat. 'regularly' takes every other letter of 'poor kid' (ORI), and 'wearing' sets everything inside the two Os of the glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large-scale sacred work for voices and orchestra, such as Handel's Messiah.

clue.text: Riddle with complex meaning any number missed

indicators.note: made complicated, so the letters are jumbled
the number is left out of the rearranged letters

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A puzzle whose intricate sense fails to include any figures.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or puzzling question, just as a riddle is.

clue.text: Quarantine accordingly delayed after source of infection

indicators.note: placed after, so it follows the opening letter
the source is where something starts, so the opening letter

parts.note: so means therefore or accordingly
late means delayed

explanation.surface: A quarantine imposed, belatedly, once the origin of an outbreak is found.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate someone is to keep them apart from others to stop disease spreading.

clue.text: Model in quiet bar popped the question

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: placed in, so the bar holds the other word

parts.note: a rod is a bar
to model is to pose for an artist

explanation.surface: A model in a quiet pub asked someone to marry them.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop the question is the idiom for asking someone to marry you, i.e. to propose.

clue.text: Schoolboys ultimately mischievous and greedy

indicators.note: in the end, so the final letter

parts.note: elfish means impish and mischievous like an elf

explanation.surface: Schoolboys turn out naughty and gluttonous in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Selfish people put themselves first, and greed is wanting more than one's share.

clue.text: A camp or billet being arranged? It's questionable

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Is setting up a military camp or lodging troops a doubtful idea?
explanation.definitionFit: Something problematical presents difficulties and is open to doubt.

clue.text: Dinner perhaps interrupted by daughter getting award

indicators.note: broken into, so the other letter sits inside

parts.note: a dinner is one example of a meal

explanation.surface: An evening meal disrupted by a girl receiving a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A medal is a metal disc given as an honour or prize.

clue.text: Support disheartened vagrant

indicators.note: with its heart, the middle, taken out

parts.note: a beggar is a homeless vagrant

explanation.surface: Backing a vagrant who has lost heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes GG, the centre of BEGGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a weight is to support it.

clue.text: Handed wine to limit pain

indicators.note: the outer word bounds the other, enclosing it

parts.note: red, a red wine
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Someone was given wine to ease their discomfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Reached, as in 'reach me the salt', means passed something over by hand.

clue.text: Reportedly regret adolescent that's tiresome

indicators.note: as reported in speech, so the phrase is heard

parts.note: rue (regret) and teen (adolescent)

explanation.surface: A grown-up is said to be sorry about a teenager who has become a bore.
explanation.definitionFit: Routine as an adjective means humdrum and monotonous, i.e. dull.

clue.text: Sentimental social media message cut short

indicators.note: with its end chopped off, losing the final letter

parts.note: a tweet, a post on Twitter (now X)

explanation.surface: A soppy online post is truncated.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee means excessively quaint or sweet, overly sentimental.

clue.text: Singer followed by good number in total

indicators.note: the next pieces come after it

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice
an anaesthetic numbs, so ether is a 'number'

explanation.surface: A singer is followed by a fine piece, making a complete set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a numeral but a thing that numbs: ether.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether means taken as a whole, overall.
